title: How long can a two-cycle quantum conveyor operate?
intro: Reader level: an undergraduate who knows the four core physics courses (classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, thermal and statistical physics) and their mathematics (linear algebra, calculus, Fourier series, complex numbers). Each question lists only what it needs beyond this level.

second-quantization.name: Fermion creation and annihilation operators
second-quantization.note: Read c†, c and n = c†c, and rewrite a hopping Hamiltonian in new modes.
second-quantization.ref: A. Altland and B. Simons, Condensed Matter Field Theory (2nd ed., Cambridge, 2010), Ch. 2 (second quantization)

bloch-matrix.name: Bloch matrix of a lattice with several sites per cell
bloch-matrix.note: Fourier-transform a chain cell by cell to get h(k), including the bond that crosses the cell boundary.
bloch-matrix.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (Springer, 2016), Sec. 1.2 (bulk Hamiltonian)

projector-calculus.name: Projectors onto a subspace
projector-calculus.note: Build p = YY† from orthonormal columns, read its rank from Tr p, and differentiate p² = p.
projector-calculus.ref: S.-M. Huang, Quantum-State Projectors on Grassmannian: Geometry, Holonomy, and Topology, arXiv:2608.06777

pauli-rotations.name: Pauli matrices, spin rotations and the Bloch sphere
pauli-rotations.note: Exponentiate a combination of Pauli matrices, and picture a spin-1/2 state as a unit vector that turns.
pauli-rotations.ref: M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (Cambridge, 2010), Sec. 4.2 (single-qubit operations)

frame-change.name: Time-dependent change of frame
frame-change.note: Transform a state with a moving unitary and find the new generator, including the term from the motion of the frame.
frame-change.ref: C. P. Slichter, Principles of Magnetic Resonance (3rd ed., Springer, 1990), Ch. 2 (the rotating frame)

wilson-loop.name: Wilson loop and multiband Wannier centres
wilson-loop.note: Multiply band-overlap matrices around the Brillouin zone and read orbital centres from the eigenphases.
wilson-loop.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (Springer, 2016), Sec. 9.1 (non-abelian Berry phase, multiband Wannier states)

tensor-commutators.name: Operators on several spins
tensor-commutators.note: Commute products of Pauli operators that act on different spins and on shared spins.
tensor-commutators.ref: M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (Cambridge, 2010), Sec. 2.1.7 (tensor products)

operator-exponentials.name: Exponentials of operators
operator-exponentials.note: Expand e^(−S) K e^(S) in nested commutators, and differentiate e^(S(t)) when S changes in time.
operator-exponentials.ref: R. M. Wilcox, Exponential operators and parameter differentiation in quantum physics, J. Math. Phys. 8, 962 (1967)

gauge-connection.name: Connections of a moving frame
gauge-connection.note: Work with A = iU†∂U for two parameters (a twist and time) and the identity that relates their derivatives.
gauge-connection.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (Springer, 2016), Sec. 2.2 (Berry connection and curvature)

partial-trace.name: Reduced density matrices and the partial trace
partial-trace.note: Trace out the rest of a chain and compute local expectation values from the reduced state.
partial-trace.ref: M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (Cambridge, 2010), Sec. 2.4.3 (the reduced density operator)

trace-norm.name: Trace distance and operator norms
trace-norm.note: Bound a difference of expectation values by the trace distance between two states.
trace-norm.ref: M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information (Cambridge, 2010), Ch. 9 (distance measures)

thouless-pump.name: Adiabatic (Thouless) pumping
thouless-pump.note: A slow periodic change of a lattice can carry particles along it, period after period.
thouless-pump.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (Springer, 2016), Ch. 4 (adiabatic charge pumping, Rice-Mele model)

wannier-centres.name: Wannier orbitals and their centres
wannier-centres.note: Localized orbitals built from a band; how the motion of their centres counts transported charge.
wannier-centres.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (Springer, 2016), Sec. 4.3 (tracking the charges with Wannier states)

band-projector.name: A group of bands as one subspace
band-projector.note: Describe bands 1 and 2 together by the plane they span at each (k, φ), without choosing a basis inside it.
band-projector.ref: S.-M. Huang, Quantum-State Projectors on Grassmannian: Geometry, Holonomy, and Topology, arXiv:2608.06777

kato-generator.name: The generator of a moving subspace
kato-generator.note: The rotation that carries a subspace along its path, and how it compares with the actual Hamiltonian.
kato-generator.ref: T. Kato, On the adiabatic theorem of quantum mechanics, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 5, 435 (1950)

adiabatic-following.name: Adiabatic following
adiabatic-following.note: When does a state follow an instantaneous eigenstate of a changing Hamiltonian? Compare the gap with the rate of change.
adiabatic-following.ref: D. J. Griffiths, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics (2nd ed., Pearson, 2005), Ch. 10 (the adiabatic approximation)

gauge-freedom.name: Basis freedom inside a group of bands
gauge-freedom.note: Separate what changes under a unitary change of basis inside the group (coordinates) from what does not (physical objects).
gauge-freedom.ref: N. Marzari, A. A. Mostofi, J. R. Yates, I. Souza, D. Vanderbilt, Maximally localized Wannier functions, Rev. Mod. Phys. 84, 1419 (2012), Sec. II

domain-models.name: Ising chains and domains
domain-models.note: Model two competing orders as two spin states; a domain is a run of the other state, and a transverse field lets spins flip.
domain-models.ref: S. Sachdev, Quantum Phase Transitions (2nd ed., Cambridge, 2011), chapter on the Ising chain in a transverse field

energy-and-transitions.name: Energy differences and transitions
energy-and-transitions.note: How a quantum system moves between states: couplings, energy conservation and transition rates.
energy-and-transitions.ref: D. J. Griffiths, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics (2nd ed., Pearson, 2005), Ch. 9 (time-dependent perturbation theory)

dressing.name: Dressing a state by a unitary (Schrieffer-Wolff)
dressing.note: Build the leading correlations into a reference state by a change of basis e^S, and expand in a small coupling.
dressing.ref: S. Bravyi, D. P. DiVincenzo, D. Loss, Schrieffer-Wolff transformation for quantum many-body systems, Ann. Phys. 326, 2793 (2011)

short-time-dynamics.name: Transition probabilities at short times
short-time-dynamics.note: How a transition probability starts at small t, and when a decay rate can be defined at all (Fermi's golden rule).
short-time-dynamics.ref: D. J. Griffiths, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics (2nd ed., Pearson, 2005), Ch. 9 (Fermi's golden rule)

locality.name: Locality in quantum many-body systems
locality.note: Local operators, overlapping local corrections, and quasi-local operators approximated in a region.
locality.ref: M. B. Hastings, Locality in Quantum Systems, arXiv:1008.5137

effective-models.name: Effective models: the kept part and the remainder
effective-models.note: Split an exact generator into a part you keep and a remainder, and ask what bounds the remainder.
effective-models.ref: S. Teufel, Adiabatic Perturbation Theory in Quantum Dynamics (Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1821, 2003)

current-operator.name: The current operator on a lattice
current-operator.note: The particle current through one bond as an operator, and its expectation value in a superposition.
current-operator.ref: J. K. Asbóth, L. Oroszlány, A. Pályi, A Short Course on Topological Insulators (Springer, 2016), Sec. 5.1 (particle current at a cross section)

twisted-boundary.name: Current from a twist (Peierls phase)
twisted-boundary.note: Put a phase e^(iθ) on one bond and obtain the current through it as −∂H/∂θ.
twisted-boundary.ref: Q. Niu, D. J. Thouless, Y.-S. Wu, Quantized Hall conductance as a topological invariant, Phys. Rev. B 31, 3372 (1985)

many-body-fidelity.name: Fidelity of a many-particle state and of its parts
many-body-fidelity.note: Compare the overlap of a whole N-particle state with the overlap of a small region of it.
many-body-fidelity.ref: W. Kohn, Nobel Lecture: Electronic structure of matter - wave functions and density functionals, Rev. Mod. Phys. 71, 1253 (1999)

open-subsystem.name: Dynamics of a subsystem
open-subsystem.note: Why the equation of motion for one region of a chain involves its couplings to the outside.
open-subsystem.ref: H.-P. Breuer and F. Petruccione, The Theory of Open Quantum Systems (Oxford, 2002), Ch. 3 (quantum master equations)

certified-bounds.name: Certified bounds and decisions with error bars
certified-bounds.note: What a sufficient bound guarantees, and how to decide with an interval instead of a single number.
certified-bounds.ref: R. E. Moore, R. B. Kearfott, M. J. Cloud, Introduction to Interval Analysis (SIAM, 2009)

prethermalization.name: Prethermalization in driven many-body systems
prethermalization.note: Why a driven interacting system can keep its order for a long but finite time, and what controls that time.
prethermalization.ref: D. Abanin, W. De Roeck, W. W. Ho, F. Huveneers, A rigorous theory of many-body prethermalization for periodically driven and closed quantum systems, Commun. Math. Phys. 354, 809 (2017)

groups.title: Problem 1: A two-cycle quantum conveyor: bands, projectors and flavors

nodes.label: 1.A.1
nodes.title: Fractional transport
nodes.note: Count the charge carried in two periods from the displacements of the occupied orbitals, and ask what fixes the single-period values.

nodes.label: 1.B.1
nodes.title: From the lattice to a projector
nodes.note: Derive the 5×5 Bloch matrix, build the projector onto bands 1 and 2, and compare three ways of counting many-particle states.

nodes.label: 1.B.2
nodes.title: From the lattice to a projector
nodes.note: Derive two identities of a moving projector and state what they say about the Hamiltonian.

nodes.label: 1.C.1
nodes.title: Following a moving projector
nodes.note: Solve one spin in a turning field exactly in a rotating frame, and find how well it follows the ground state.

nodes.label: 1.D.1
nodes.title: A plane is not yet a flavor
nodes.note: Separate basis changes inside a plane from physical changes of flavor, and ask what a Wilson loop or a determinant can decide.

groups.title: Problem 2: Correlations and the physical current

nodes.label: 2.A.1
nodes.title: Domains in a spin chain
nodes.note: Find the energy of a domain in a spin chain, and ask whether a lower energy forces the domain to form.

nodes.label: 2.B.1
nodes.title: Dressing a reference state
nodes.note: Solve a two-level cluster: its dressed ground state, and the exact dynamics that starts from the bare state.

nodes.label: 2.B.2
nodes.title: Dressing a reference state
nodes.note: Compute what appears when local corrections on neighbouring clusters overlap.

nodes.label: 2.C.1
nodes.title: Exact frames and kept dynamics
nodes.note: Derive the exact generator in a dressed moving frame, and find where the first approximation enters.

nodes.label: 2.C.2
nodes.title: Exact frames and kept dynamics
nodes.note: Find when the kept dynamics preserves a reference direction, and test it on the spin chain at short times.

nodes.label: 2.D.1
nodes.title: The physical current
nodes.note: Compute the current in a superposition of two states, and ask what a probability alone can tell.

nodes.label: 2.D.2
nodes.title: The physical current
nodes.note: Transform the current operator to a moving frame and integrate it over time.

groups.title: Problem 3: How long can the conveyor operate?

nodes.label: 3.A.1
nodes.title: Local accuracy in a large system
nodes.note: Compare the fidelity of a whole product state with the fidelity of a small region of it.

nodes.label: 3.A.2
nodes.title: Local accuracy in a large system
nodes.note: Bound the error of a local current by the distance between two reduced states.

nodes.label: 3.A.3
nodes.title: Local accuracy in a large system
nodes.note: Derive the equation of motion of a region's state, and identify what it needs from outside the region.

nodes.label: 3.B.1
nodes.title: A conditional operating-time certificate
nodes.note: Integrate supplied local bounds over a two-period window, and find the time up to which they certify the charge.

nodes.label: 3.C.1
nodes.title: Prediction, error and first failure
nodes.note: Turn a prediction with an error bar into tests for single windows, and apply them to three sample windows.

nodes.label: 3.C.2
nodes.title: Prediction, error and first failure
nodes.note: List what must be derived from the real pump before the tests apply, and ask what locating the first failure needs.

footer: Main line: the 18 questions in exam order. Left, blue: computation tools (mathematics you calculate with). Right, orange: modelling ideas (physics you reason with). Each item appears in full where it is first needed and as a dashed reminder later. Tick an item when you can use it without looking it up.
The toolbox appendix of the solutions (Appendix D) works the smallest example of each tool that the question paper states without proof.
